source_review.notes: Checked current official CMU SEI ATAM method and collection pages, including scenarios, risks, sensitivity points, trade-off points, and risk themes; the current NASA Systems Engineering Handbook decision-analysis and trade-study guidance; current ISO 31000:2018 status; and ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 metadata. Multiobjective foundations were reviewed against the cited monographs.

evidence: Reviewed feasible set F, outcome functions, dominance relation, Pareto efficiency, weighted additive utility model, normalized value functions, weights, parameter set, and robustness definition.
Confirmed favorable direction, quantifiers, domains, nonnegative weights, unit-sum constraint, and model qualifications.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates raw outcomes from preference transformations and handles hard constraints outside compensating utility.

evidence: Recomputed U(A)=0.5 times 0.8 plus 0.3 times 0.5 plus 0.2 times 0.9 equals 0.73.
Recomputed U(B)=0.5 times 0.6 plus 0.3 times 0.9 plus 0.2 times 0.7 equals 0.71.
Checked dominance examples A=(8,6,5) over B=(7,6,4) and A=(7,8,5) over B=(7,6,5).
numerical_recomputation.notes: The narrow score difference is correctly presented as sensitivity evidence, not an objective verdict.

evidence: Checked that the dominance definition requires weak superiority on every considered objective and strict superiority on at least one.
Confirmed that Pareto efficiency excludes feasible dominators and that weighted utility assumes declared transformations and compensability.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: All formal conclusions are explicitly relative to the feasible set, objectives, scenarios, transformations, evidence, and parameter ranges.

evidence: Reviewed hard constraints, missing evidence, correlated criteria, rank reversal, status quo cost, common-cause regional failure, cache states, supplier benchmarks, lifecycle transitions, uneven stakeholder harm, and emergency-triage and evacuation transfer.
Tested dominance conclusions against omitted criteria and uncertainty and preserved non-compensable duties outside scoring.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The chapter challenges technical, organizational, lifecycle, authority, distributional, and high-consequence decision boundaries.

evidence: Traced common comparison scope, coherent alternatives, traceable criteria, explicit units, constraints before compensation, raw evidence preservation, visible uncertainty, sensitivity analysis, distributional visibility, authorized decision, and lifecycle review through exposition, examples, and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: Scoring and dominance never replace stakeholder legitimacy, domain authority, or residual-risk acceptance.

evidence: Reviewed both numerical dominance examples against the quantified definition and checked the Pareto-set answer.
Reviewed weighted-sum premises and confirmed that robustness over Theta is not claimed as universal optimality.
proof_review.notes: The chapter presents definitions and conditional model conclusions rather than a proof that any architecture is universally best.

evidence: Audited uses of proof, objective, optimal, robust, complete, dominance, feasible, evidence, validation, and decision.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is offered; all optimality-like terms are bounded to explicit models.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No experiment, benchmark, executable snippet, or newly measured empirical result is presented. Prototype, supplier, field, and operational evidence are discussed only as bounded evidence sources.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed framing, alternatives, criteria, feasibility, dominance, Pareto efficiency, scoring assumptions, uncertainty, sensitivity, quality interactions, lifecycle economics, decision authority, and reopening for conceptual coherence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed synchronous/asynchronous validation, caching, regional topologies, shared platforms, supplier evidence, status quo, prototypes, migration, exit, operational burden, and residual risk. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from decision framing through formal comparison, sensitivity, failure modes, ten distinct examples, and five complete answers culminating in unfamiliar evacuation-routing transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
